analysis_notes.source_text_analysis:
Torah #261 is a two-sentence aphorism (Likutay Moharan Volume 1). The full text is:

'כְּשֶׁנּוֹפֵל אָדָם מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ, יֵדַע שֶׁמִּן הַשָּׁמַיִם הוּא, כִּי הִתְרַחֲקוּת – תְּחִלַּת הִתְקָרְבוּת, עַל־כֵּן נָפַל, שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר יוֹתֵר לְהִתְקָרֵב לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וַעֲצָתוֹ – שֶׁיַּתְחִיל מֵחָדָשׁ לִכָּנֵס בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא הִתְחִיל עֲדַיִן כְּלָל מֵעוֹלָם. וְזֶה כְּלָל גָּדוֹל בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם, שֶׁצְּרִיכִין מַמָּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם לְהַתְחִיל מֵחָדָשׁ.'

The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in this text. All logical connections are eitza (causal-teleological):
- הִתְרַחֲקוּת → הִתְקָרְבוּת: 'distance is the beginning of closeness' reads as teleological causation, not conceptual identity. The Rebbe states that distance is *purposefully designed* to produce closeness — one thing leads to another, not: 'distance IS closeness in its essence.' This is directional/functional, not bechina.
- נְפִילָה (falling) → הִתְעוֹרְרוּת (arousal to draw close): explicitly eitza — 'he fell SO THAT he would be aroused' (שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר).
- הַתְחָלָה מֵחָדָשׁ (fresh start) is the eitza advice, not a bechina equivalence.

No gap exists because no packages exist. There are no missing bechina concepts to flag.

eitza_relationships_in_source_text.relationship: eitza — divine purpose: the fall is arranged so that it generates arousal for return; distance is not the same essence as closeness but rather produces/enables it
